title: Legacy CRM Administration and Configuration Reference
summary: Administrator configuration reference covering account management setup, licensing administration, scheduling optimization, organizational relationships, regulatory compliance, and strategic account planning capabilities within the legacy CRM platform.

findings.account_address_management: Multi-address support for healthcare professional and organization accounts with configurable display formats. Address management includes: primary/secondary designation, address validation workflows with responsible user assignments, geographic coordinate storage for territory alignment and route optimization, and address sharing across affiliated accounts. Administrators configure which address fields display on mobile and web interfaces through layout configuration.
findings.license_administration: Three distinct license tracking domains: healthcare professional state licensing (medical license verification with expiration tracking and renewal alerts), distributor licensing (controlled substance distribution authorization), and federal registration numbers (DEA license tracking for prescribing authority verification). Each domain supports configurable validation rules, expiration warning thresholds, and compliance reporting. License data integrates with call compliance to prevent interactions with unlicensed practitioners.
findings.scheduling_optimization: Configurable contact scheduling preferences including: preferred contact time windows per account (morning, afternoon, specific hours), day-of-week preferences, channel preferences (in-person, phone, video), and seasonal availability patterns. Admin console provides parameter configuration for how scheduling suggestions surface to field representatives. The feature supports upgrade activation workflows where existing implementations can enable enhanced scheduling after platform updates.
findings.affiliation_management: Organizational relationship tracking between healthcare professionals and institutions (hospitals, clinics, group practices, academic medical centers). Features include: bidirectional affiliation with role mapping (attending physician, department head, researcher), network visualization showing institutional hierarchies, product-level affiliation filtering, uniqueness validation preventing duplicate relationship records, configurable record type and product filters on network views, and summary views aggregating affiliation data across territories.
findings.compliance_framework: Regulatory compliance tracking for healthcare engagement rules (interaction limits, cooling periods, reporting requirements). Configuration includes: compliance template definitions with rule parameters, compliance cycle management (annual, quarterly, per-product), survey-based compliance verification, job scheduling for automated compliance calculations, and prioritization logic for compliance cycle vs. to-do updates based on survey type. Supports both Engagement Policy for Pharmaceutical Visits (EPPV) and Medical Information Delivery (MID) compliance models.
findings.account_planning: Strategic account planning capabilities for key account management: account plan creation with or without specific account linkage (supporting portfolio-level plans), situational analysis components (with both legacy Aura and current LWC implementations), stakeholder management with mapping to account plan team members, objective tracking with linkage to field activities (calls), to-do management with Kanban visualization, cross-organizational sharing for global accounts, survey integration for plan assessment, and CSV import capabilities for bulk to-do and stakeholder data loading.
findings.dynamic_list_management: Configurable account list views with advanced filtering capabilities: dynamic lists (saved filter configurations), bulk account selection and action operations, field-level filter definitions, time-based filtering (scheduling windows), search-before-create workflows for duplicate prevention (with master data management integration options and external registry search), and account export from filtered views. Permissions govern which users can create and manage dynamic list definitions.
findings.admin_console_architecture: Centralized administration interface built on custom metadata-driven menu configuration. Menu items are dynamically constructed from metadata records, enabling feature-specific administration pages without code deployment. The admin console provides parameter management for scheduling, compliance, territory alignment, content management, and integration configuration across the platform.

source: CRM Configuration Technical Guide (July 2024, Document Version 1.0)
